opportunities.title: Cisco Foundation Global Impact Cash Grants - Climate Resilience priority sector (incl. regenerative agriculture); year-round LOI
opportunities.program: Cisco Global Impact Cash Grants (Climate Resilience)
opportunities.deadline_text: We accept applications year-round from eligible organizations.
opportunities.funding_text: The maximum request amount for first-time grant recipients is US$100,000.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: US 501(c)(3) public charities; non-US organizations that are 'the equivalent of a U.S. public charity' (determined from submitted documents). Program audience must be >65% economically underserved. Overhead not to exceed 25% (case-by-case exceptions). Excludes hospitals, healthcare, schools, scholarships, events, grant-making foundations.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Global (non-US organizations eligible if equivalent to a US public charity)
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT is an international organization and Bioversity International an Italian-registered international non-profit; whether either passes Cisco's 'equivalent of a U.S. public charity' determination is unconfirmed. Alternatives: apply via a US-registered 501(c)(3) partner or support a national NGO partner as lead.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Pass online eligibility quiz in Cisco Grants portal; LOI; full proposal by invitation only.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: None stated; audience must be >65% economically underserved.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Climate Resilience: 'education, regenerative agriculture, conservation, protection, and clean energy solutions'.
opportunities.application_procedure: 1) Eligibility quiz on Cisco Grants and Cash Donations portal; 2) LOI via portal (review may take up to one business quarter); 3) Full proposal by invitation; decision within one business quarter.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Regenerative/resilient agriculture for underserved communities fits climate-smart ag and digital advisory delivery, but Cisco funds implementation/scale more than research; RS/AI would be enabling tools.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Global tech-corporate funder with year-round intake; could fund a smallholder digital climate-advisory pilot in LAC/Africa.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team can deliver digital advisory/climate-smart ag pilots; main hurdle is entity eligibility; 65% underserved-audience requirement easily met in smallholder settings.
opportunities.recommendation: Worth a quick eligibility-quiz test with the Bioversity/CIAT entity; if it fails, pair with a national NGO or US 501(c)(3) partner. Modest size (<= USD 100k first grant) - suitable for a pilot or to co-fund staff time on a digital advisory deployment (staff eligibility not stated).
opportunities.potential_partners: National farmer organizations / NGOs in Colombia, Honduras, Kenya; US-registered charities
opportunities.next_action: Run the Cisco Grants portal eligibility quiz using Bioversity International details; if eligible, draft LOI on AI-enabled climate advisory for smallholders.

evidence.status_quote: We accept applications year-round from eligible organizations.
evidence.staff_costs_quote: Not specified (only: 'An organization's overhead is not to exceed 25 percent')

opportunities.title: OpenAI Foundation USD 60M AI weather & crop-disease forecasting for smallholders (grantees selected; CIMMYT among them) - partner pathway
opportunities.deadline_text: No application process; grantees were selected.
opportunities.funding_text: $60 million effort to 'support government-led efforts to deliver weather and crop disease forecasts to 100 million smallholder farmers' over three years (total portfolio, not per grant).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Selected organizations only: University of Chicago, UC Berkeley, Precision Development, AIM for Scale (via University of Notre Dame), Digital Green, CIMMYT.
opportunities.eligible_countries: South and Southeast Asia, East Africa
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIMMYT (CGIAR) is a direct grantee, showing CGIAR centers are fundable by this funder. Alliance route: sub-award/collaboration via CIMMYT, AIM for Scale or Digital Green; watch for follow-on open calls.
opportunities.eligible_activities: AI-powered weather and crop-disease forecasts delivered through government-led systems.
opportunities.application_procedure: No open call; contact via the email link on the page or through grantee consortium.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Core match: AI forecasting, crop modelling, climate advisory for smallholders.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Major new tech-philanthropy funder in the CGIAR space; sister center already funded.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has crop modelling, EO and digital advisory expertise in East Africa and Asia.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue as partner: approach CIMMYT and AIM for Scale to offer EO/crop-modelling components; monitor OpenAI Foundation for follow-on calls.
opportunities.potential_partners: CIMMYT, AIM for Scale, Digital Green, Precision Development
opportunities.next_action: Contact the CIMMYT lead for the OpenAI-funded forecasting work about an Alliance contribution (sub-award).

evidence.deadline_quote: (none) 'The Foundation selected these organizations for their leadership in their respective areas of work.'
evidence.eligibility_quote: University of Chicago, UC Berkeley, Precision Development, AIM for Scale, Digital Green, CIMMYT

opportunities.verification_notes: Official openaifoundation.org news page loaded 2026-11-02. Distinct from existing Gates/Google.org USD 100M record (different funder).

opportunities.title: Danone Ecosystem - co-created partnerships for regenerative agriculture / inclusive food systems (no open call; contact-based)
opportunities.deadline_text: No open call; 'Reach out to co-create' (ecosystem@danone.com).
opportunities.funding_text: Funding can come through 'grants, blended finance, or parallel funding'. No amounts stated.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Co-funders (foundations, development banks, public donors, impact investors); NGOs/local organizations; 'field-based experts and organizations that bring practical, proven know-how' (technical/knowledge partners).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT/Bioversity would enter as technical/knowledge partner on a Danone-sourcing-linked project (e.g., regenerative dairy/agriculture landscapes), not via an open call.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Regenerative agriculture (nature mission), watershed protection, inclusive plastic collection; agriculture, waste/water, health.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Regenerative-agriculture MRV and landscape monitoring with EO plus crop/soil modelling are directly useful to supply-chain programs.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Corporate agri-food funder able to co-finance multi-year field programs; LAC and Africa presence.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: EO-based regenerative-agriculture monitoring is within team capabilities.
opportunities.recommendation: Partnership lead rather than a call. Propose an EO/AI regenerative-agriculture MRV component for a Danone Ecosystem project in LAC.
opportunities.potential_partners: Danone Mexico/Brazil sourcing teams; local dairy cooperatives
opportunities.next_action: Send a short concept note to ecosystem@danone.com via the Alliance partnerships office.

evidence.eligibility_quote: field-based experts and organizations that bring practical, proven know-how
evidence.status_quote: No open calls listed; contact ecosystem@danone.com

opportunities.title: Shoots by Syngenta - live open-innovation challenges (Soil restoration solutions; Biological solutions for crop performance under drought stress)
opportunities.deadline_text: No closing date stated; listed as live challenges.
opportunities.funding_text: 'We are able to fund selected projects to drive toward commercialization.' Terms case by case; no amounts stated.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Syngenta wants to 'collaborate with academia, start-ups, and industry'; no formal eligibility rules published.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No restriction stated; CIAT/Bioversity could submit an idea as a research institute. Commercialization/IP terms would need review against CGIAR IP principles.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Submit an idea via the challenge 'Submit an idea' form.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Soil restoration: soil-applied chemical/physical/biological technologies improving soil function with measurable improvement within a few seasons. Drought: biological technologies (microbials, natural products, peptides, RNA, extracts) with proof of concept under water deficit; GE/GM out of scope.
opportunities.application_procedure: Online idea submission per challenge; Syngenta follows up on selected ideas.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Challenges seek product technologies acting on soil/plants; RS/AI monitoring or modelling appears out of scope (inference). Relevant only if Alliance soil teams have a soil-applied technology, with RS/phenotyping for efficacy evaluation.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Corporate agri partner that can fund research, but commercialization focus fits CGIAR poorly.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires a candidate product; our team would contribute monitoring/phenotyping only.
opportunities.recommendation: Low priority for this researcher; forward to Alliance soils/biochar colleagues.
opportunities.next_action: Forward challenge links to Alliance soils team; no action for RS/AI group unless a product partner emerges.

evidence.eligibility_quote: collaborate with academia, start-ups, and industry

opportunities.verification_notes: Official shootsbysyngenta.com challenge list and two challenge pages loaded 2026-11-02. The separate Syngenta Foundation for Sustainable Agriculture (Basel) is in liquidation - no calls.
